# dsh-coding-discipline

An always-on coding-discipline layer for DeepSeek Harness. It does not add tools or
call the model t

wice — it changes what the model is told to treat as acceptable
work, on every step, and ships a lon

ger protocol the model can load when a task
deserves it.
## What it targets
Each rule names one failure mode that costs real time in long coding sessions:
| Rule | Failure it prevents |

| `ledger` | Constraints stated early ("don't touch the public API") get dropped 40 turns later |
|

`proof` | "已完成 / 应该没问题" without a build or test run in that turn |
| `smallest-diff` | A 3-line chan

ge rewritten as a whole-file replacement, with unrelated churn |
| `hypothesis` | Guess-and-patch lo

ops on linker/ABI/runtime bugs instead of a discriminating experiment |
| `no-invented-apis` | Plaus

ible-looking flags, signatures and config keys that do not exist |
| `finish-migration` | Refactors

that leave one call site on the old path |
| `evidence-over-agreeing` | Editing working code because

the user said "this looks wrong" |
| `no-speculative-code` | Abstractions, parameters and defensive

branches nobody asked for |
| `closing-shape` | Reports that celebrate instead of stating what chan
ged, what ran, what is unverified |

## Verify it loaded
After restart, the section is part of every request. Either:

- ask the model to restate its `<coding_discipline>` rules — it should quote them;
- or run the pack
age's own tests: `node --test` (22 tests, no DSH needed).

If the app fails to start after install, remove the single `"dsh-coding-discipline"`
line from `dsh.
profile.bundles` and restart — nothing else is touched.
## The effect dashboard

Two ways to see whether the rules change anything, both reading the same
analysis over persisted ses
sion logs (`~/.dsh/sessions/**/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
What it measures:
| Metric | How it is computed |
| 改动-验证闭环率 | turns containing an edit/write tool call **and** a verification command in the same tur

n, over all editing turns |
| 无证据的完成声明 | turns whose closing message claims completion while no veri

fication command ran that turn |
| 代价 | tool calls per turn, answer characters per turn |

Grouping is by **turn**, decided by whether that turn's system prompt contains
`<coding_discipline>`

— not by date, so a session that started before the install
contributes its later turns to the trea

date, so a session that started before the install
contributes its later turns to the treatment arm.

There is no randomisation and the baseline is your own history. The page says so
in a banner and aga

in in the method note; it answers "did the behaviour change",
not "is the model better".

## Limits

- It is prompt influence, not enforcement: a model can still ignore a rule. The
rules are phrased as

triggers ("before the first edit", "two speculative edits
in a row") because trigger-shaped instruc

tions survive long sessions better
than general virtues.
- It applies to every agent in the composit

ion, including subagents.
- It does not verify your build for you; it makes an unverified claim expl

including subagents.
- It does not verify your build for you; it makes an unverified claim explicit.
